question: Does the open TRL #6637 KL overflow guard preserve a positive clipped K3 KL value and corrective gradient when the configured positive clip underflows to zero in the working dtype?

estimand.objective: beta*K3(x), beta=0.1, zero policy advantage, token-level importance ratio equal to one
estimand.gradient: d loss / d current-policy token log-probability; for x>0 it must remain strictly negative when the finite upper clip is active, so optimization moves the policy toward the reference

frozen_cases.name: candidate_accepted_tiny_positive_clip_float16
frozen_cases.expected: audit whether configured clip casts to zero and silently yields zero KL and zero gradient

frozen_cases.name: candidate_representable_clip_float16_control
frozen_cases.expected: finite positive K3 loss and strictly negative finite loss gradient

method: Import the exact production GRPOTrainer._compute_loss method from each clean pinned source revision and invoke it directly on CPU with a one-token leaf log-probability fixture, fake accelerator reductions, zero advantages, and beta=0.1. Separately construct GRPOConfig with the tiny positive clip to establish whether configuration accepts it. Do not copy or reimplement the loss equation in the primary runner.
failure_criteria: source code or commit differs from the frozen base or candidate
the exact production loss method cannot be invoked without altering source
fixture enables nonzero policy loss or an importance ratio other than one
result omits the config acceptance outcome or finite/non-finite loss and gradient fields
interpretation_limits: This audits an edge case in an open numerical-stability PR; it does not establish behavior prevalence in real training workloads.
A finite control fixture is not model training or task capability evidence.
The PR already addresses the main K3 overflow issue; this study only checks representability of a user-supplied clip after conversion to the working dtype.
The study does not test the Liger fused path, GPU kernels, or all mixed-precision/autocast combinations.
